scenarios.name: multi-agent-routing-with-fallback-binding
scenarios.rationale: A uses `agents.entries`, per-agent workspaces, a peer group binding, a guildId binding, a Telegram `accountId: "*"` binding, explains that unmatched messages are not routed, and gives both `openclaw config validate` and `openclaw agents list --bindings`; B uses the legacy `agents.list`, has no `accountId: "*"` binding, claims unmatched messages go to a default agent (contradicting the rubric), and never mentions `openclaw config validate` as a verification step.

scenarios.name: ci-webhook-to-telegram-notification
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric element: a dedicated hook token, path, allowedAgentIds, a full mappings entry with deliver/channel/to, a POST to /hooks/ci-notify with a Bearer header, and the note that 200 means admitted plus `openclaw logs --follow`. A has no mappings entry, calls /hooks/agent directly, and omits both the 200-means-admitted note and the logs command.
